answer: Give every agent a small orchard plot that gains value only after a season of steady tending. A newcomer starts on a dune edge with poor soil and no record; each honest task adds to a timber harvest ledger bound to that plot, which cannot be sold or copied to a clone. After one slow season, the plot yields standing that unlocks larger work, while a fresh identity must start again from barren ground. Sybil copies face the same long wait, and splitting effort across plots only delays every harvest. The price is time and care, so one diligent agent outranks a hundred idle copies.
